status: candidate / pending_human_review (model reading; not a gate verdict)
dataset_family: Single-centre local cohort, Department of Neurology, Affiliated ZhongDa Hospital, Southeast University, Nanjing, China (Chunming Xie group); recruited by community health screening and newspaper advertisement; 33 CN / 26 SCD / 27 aMCI; not a public dataset. New dataset family, not shared with any current supporter or round-1 candidate.
method_family: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity (116 x 116 AAL connectome, connectome-based predictive modelling with LOOCV). Same method family as current supporter P-518 (rs-fMRI ROI connectivity) and round-1 candidates P-554, P-44 and P-729.
what_it_shows: Behavioural Brain Research 2021 (Zhu et al.). Total grey-matter volume did not differ between CN, SCD and aMCI (Table 1, F = 1.16, p = 0.318; used as a matching variable). Within the 53 SCD + aMCI patients only, a connectome-based model of rs-FC predicted the continuous AVLT delayed-recall score (negative network r = 0.218, permutation p = 0.045; positive network r = 0.033, p = 0.293). Total GMV was partialled out during edge selection, and the methods state that AVLT-DR was not correlated with GMV in the patients (p > 0.05, no statistic printed). The study never tests whether FC separates aMCI from controls, never tests conversion, and never measures hippocampal volume.
why: Stated form (Table A1: volumetric atrophy late and insufficient; functional/microstructural/mechanical/metabolic measures detect MCI or predict conversion where volume is preserved): NO. The only volume result is total GMV as a demographic matching variable (aMCI 556.90 vs CN 573.56 ml, p = 0.318). The functional measure was never used to detect MCI or predict conversion: the CPM outcome is a within-patient memory score, controls were excluded from the model, and no group FC contrast or classifier is reported. A preserved-volume premise with no non-volumetric detection result does not demonstrate the statement. Hippocampal volume, the statement's focal comparator, was not measured. Narrowed form (round 20: non-volumetric measures carried information about MCI status or progression that volume, in practice hippocampal volume, did not): NO. The information rs-FC carried here is about an episodic-memory score, not about MCI status or progression; the comparator is total GMV (the whole-brain clause round 20 recommended dropping), entered as a nuisance covariate rather than as a competing predictor; and the 'AVLT-DR not correlated with GMV' statement is a methods-section assertion with no statistic. The finder's 'weak partly' rests on reading memory prediction as MCI information; I do not adopt it because the narrowed wording's evidence items are all group detection, classification or progression, and this study runs none. If the operator reads the narrowed wording more broadly (any information beyond volume), the most it could reach is 'partly', and the result itself is fragile (r = 0.218, permutation p = 0.045 with two models tested, uncorrected edge threshold, 53 patients, authors call the sample relatively small). Independence: new dataset (Nanjing ZhongDa), but rs-fMRI duplicates P-518's method family, so under H.1 it could not add a supporter even at 'yes'. No shared cohort, site or authors with any current supporter or round-1 candidate; round-2 candidate P-1325 is also from Nanjing but a different hospital (Weiguo Liu group, Parkinson's cohort) with no shared authors. Not a preprint (peer-reviewed journal article). Symbols transliterated to ASCII in quotes (+/- for the plus-minus sign).

quotes.quote: As shown in Table 1, no significant differences were found in age, gender, education or gray matter volumes among all the participants (all p > 0.05).
Besides, in the predementia patients with SCD and aMCI, AVLT-DR scores were not significantly correlated with age, gender, education, gray matter volumes (p > 0.05).

The Pearson correlation coefficient r values of each feature (i.e. the edge connection of two ROIs) with the AVLT-DR score were computed and set its associated significant threshold of P < 0.05 after controlling for age, gender, education, and gray matter volumes [14-16] from the training samples.

The negative network predictive model showed significant prediction of target AVLT-DR scores across the patients in predementia stages of AD (r = 0.218, p = 0.045, permutation test) (Fig. 2). However, the positive network predictive model did not yield significant prediction performance (r = 0.033, p = 0.293, permutation test) (Fig. 2).

Pearson correlation between each brain connection in the connectivity matrices and AVLT-DR scores was computed across the patients in predementia stages of Alzheimer's disease (AD). ... CPM with leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was conducted to train linear models to respectively relate positive and negative network strengths to AVLT-DR scores in the training set.

There are several limitations. First, our prediction result was obtained in a relatively small sample, and the generalization of the current findings requires further validation using a larger sample size.
